text:
drew: noticed a burst of reconnects in us-west-2 right after the console auto-fallback rollout. reconnects ~4x for ~9m, and dashboards show many of these as ERROR-level resume failures even though clients were auto-fallbacked to a degraded model. anyone else see this?
isha: yep, caught it on the stream-monitor board. the fallback path closes the original session and opens a new one which our billing pipeline interprets as a new session start. thats the duplicate-charge vector.
cam: console change: we flipped fallback-mode from \"in-place\" -> \"recreate\" to simplify state. i thought billing would de-dupe, but apparently it doesn't.
drew: sample logs:```text
2026-09-05T14:02:11Z INFO fallback invoked route=low-cost-variant cause=model-unavailable session=abc123
2026-09-05T14:02:11Z INFO session closed reason=fallback-recreate session=abc123
2026-09-05T14:02:12Z INFO session opened sid=def456 client=52.23.11.5 billing_flag=new_open
```
kyle: oof. console also reclassified these events as resume_failures in telemetry because the fallback happened during resume handshake. that contaminated our canary dashboards and caused an automated alert.
deploy-bot: rollout event: console-fallback v2 -> 2026-09-05T14:00:00Z :rocket:
ops-bot: alert: reconnect-spike us-west-2 detected 2026-09-05T14:03:00Z (mag 4x)
isha: immediate mitigation: toggle console fallback-mode back to \"in-place\" for us-west-2 and mute the afflicted alert. low blast.
drew: i'm toggling now and pausing rollout globally. will also add a temporary mapping in billing to treat sequential close+open within 5s as resume-candidate for charge dedupe.
kyle: quick fix is fine, but we need telemetry hygiene. propose adding metrics: stream.fallback.invoked, stream.fallback.recreate_count, stream.fallback.inplace_count and a trace annotation fallback.mode. console can surface these in rollout view.\am: cam: +1 to metrics. also add an explicit event stream.rollout.impact that lists whether fallback-mode changes were included in the rollout so oncall can see risk pre-deploy.
drew: billing note: creating BILL-721 for provisional credits and alerting support. @billing-bot
billing-bot: created BILL-721 provisional adjustments queued.
cam: design question: is \"recreate\" fallback ever necessary? original rationale was avoiding long-lived in-memory state when switching variants, but it seems too disruptive for live traffic.
isha: maybe make recreate fallback opt-in per-tenant. default in-place, with an escape hatch for very stateful customers that need a clean env. product/console should show per-tenant fallback preference in the rollout diff.
kyle: long-term: make fallback reattachable: emit a resume proof that the new session can claim the previous session id for accounting and state linkage without re-executing model warmup. that would avoid billing noise and reduce cold-starts. ticket INFRA-1600.\am: cam: also add a canary gate: if stream.fallback.recreate_count > 0 AND stream.auth.resume_reject_rate > 0.2% -> auto-pause rollout. we want to catch these combos.
drew: for postmortem instrumentation: add stream.resume.relabelled_count when telemetry mislabels fallback-caused reconnects as resume failures. we'll backfill corrections for dashboards.
isha: console UX: add a pre-deploy warning when toggling fallback mode: \"Changing fallback to \"recreate\" can cause session churn and billing events. Recommend in-place for live traffic.\" create CONSOLE-594.\am: cam: i'm drafting the RFC to change default and add metrics and gating. INFRA-1600 (reattachable-fallback), CONSOLE-594 (pre-deploy warning + per-tenant toggle), SRE-3310 (canary gate), BILL-721 (billing reconciliation).
drew: mitigation applied and reconnects returned to baseline. i'll collect timeline and write the incident note. paste short facts here if i missed anything. :memo:
